context: systems-integration-led · ventilation/smoke-control & vertical transport gate handover

brief.intro: New to this project type? A metro station is a below- or at-grade transit building whose civil box — diaphragm walls, platform and concourse slabs — is only the shell. What actually governs the programme is fitting out and proving the station's life-safety and passenger systems: tunnel/station ventilation that clears smoke in a fire, escalators, lifts and platform screen doors that move passengers safely, and the fire, security and passenger-information systems tied together by SCADA. Because a station sits inside a wider metro line, its systems must also integrate with line-wide signalling, power and control-centre systems commissioned outside the station's own contract. The critical path typically runs from civil box handover through MEP fit-out into a long, staged systems-integration and trial-running programme before the station can open to passengers.

scope.name: Station box civil works
scope.desc: Diaphragm walls, excavation and the structural base, concourse and platform slabs.

scope.name: Waterproofing & tanking
scope.desc: Protecting the below-grade box against groundwater ingress before internal fit-out starts.

scope.name: Architectural fit-out
scope.desc: Platform/concourse finishes, cladding, ceilings and public-area walls and floors.

scope.name: Ventilation & HVAC
scope.desc: Tunnel and station ventilation (TVS/ECS) for smoke control, plus concourse and back-of-house air conditioning.

scope.name: Electrical power & lighting
scope.desc: Station power supply and distribution, normal/essential/UPS lighting, and earthing.

scope.name: Fire & life safety
scope.desc: Detection, suppression and the fire cause-and-effect logic that links a fire event to the station's automatic response.

scope.name: Vertical transportation
scope.desc: Escalators, lifts and platform screen doors that move passengers between levels and onto the platform.

scope.name: ELV, security & passenger systems
scope.desc: CCTV, access control, automatic fare collection (AFC) and public address/passenger information (PA/PIS).

scope.name: BMS / SCADA integration
scope.desc: The station control system tying MEP and life-safety systems together, and integrating with the line-wide control centre.

scope.name: Testing, systems integration & trial running
scope.desc: Proving every system individually, then together, before an extended trial-running period ahead of opening.

glossary.plain: Tunnel Ventilation System / Environmental Control System — the fans and dampers that control airflow and clear smoke in a fire.
glass doors along the platform edge that only open once a train is correctly berthed.
Automatic Fare Collection — the gates and ticketing equipment passengers use to enter and exit.
Passenger Information System / Public Address — the screens and speakers that inform passengers.
the tested logic linking a fire or smoke detection event to the exact automatic response — fans start, doors release, dampers open.
current that leaks from the train's traction-return system into the ground or structure and can corrode reinforcement — controlled by earthing and bonding.
the local control point through which all station systems are monitored and, in an emergency, overridden.
an extended period the finished station operates as if in passenger service, to prove reliability before opening.

must_get_right: Ventilation and fire cause-and-effect is the system that gates handover — build real time into the schedule for the integrated smoke-control test, not just individual system tests.
Escalators, lifts and platform screen doors are long-lead, factory-tested equipment whose delivery and installation sequence drives the fit-out programme.

The station does not commission in isolation — passenger systems (AFC, PIS, SCADA) and traction/earthing must integrate with the wider line, so interface dates with the systemwide contractor are schedule constraints, not internal milestones.
Waterproofing and tanking must be proven before internal fit-out starts — a leak found after finishes are in is a costly rework loop.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. The station schedule interfaces with the wider line-wide master schedule through constrained milestones for civil handover and systems-integration access.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Civil box works run an extended-shift, 6-day calendar to protect handover to MEP; fit-out and systems-integration works run controlled-access shifts once track and traction power are live nearby, governed by rail possession/track-access windows.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs station box & waterproofing → MEP rough-in → ventilation & fire systems set → vertical transportation install → systems integration → integrated fire/smoke cause-and-effect test → trial running → handover. Vertical transportation delivery and the integrated smoke-control/fire C&E test are the classic late-programme bottlenecks.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: The civil box is handed over dry and to tolerance; line-wide systems (traction power, signalling, SCADA) are available for integration testing per the interface schedule; a single fit-out mobilisation; authority (fire and rail regulator) approvals are staged with design freeze.

sections.heading: Procurement & long-lead items
sections.body: The schedule is procurement-led on passenger and life-safety equipment. The following are tracked as milestones and drive the network:

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: The worksite sits inside or adjacent to a live or soon-to-be-live rail corridor: possession/track-access windows, confined below-grade access, and shared laydown with the systemwide contractor all constrain work; specialist commissioning resources (ventilation, fire C&E, SCADA) are shared across stations on the line.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: late civil handover, vertical-transportation delivery slippage, cause-and-effect re-test loops, and interface delays with the line-wide systems contractor. Schedule contingency is held before the integrated systems test and trial running rather than spread across rough-in activities.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client/operator; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for MEP and systems trades — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
